passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel antioxidant compound, Antiox-7, on oxidative stress markers in adult mice. In a randomized controlled trial, 120 mice were divided into three groups: a control group receiving a standard diet (n=40), a low-dose group receiving 10 mg/kg Antiox-7 (n=40), and a high-dose group receiving 30 mg/kg Antiox-7 (n=40). After 12 weeks, plasma malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were measured as an index of lipid peroxidation. The control group had a mean MDA of 12.5 µmol/L (SD 1.2). The low-dose group had a mean of 9.8 µmol/L (SD 1.0), and the high-dose group had a mean of 7.6 µmol/L (SD 0.9). The investigators reported a dose-dependent reduction in MDA, with a statistically significant difference between the control and high-dose groups (p<0.001). The study suggests Antiox-7 may mitigate oxidative damage in vivo.
stem: Which of the following best describes the pattern of MDA levels observed in the study?

options.A: MDA levels increased with higher Antiox-7 doses.
options.B: MDA levels were unchanged across all groups.
options.C: MDA levels decreased in a dose-dependent manner.
options.D: Only the low-dose group showed a significant reduction in MDA.

explanation: The data show a progressive decline in mean MDA from control (12.5) to low-dose (9.8) to high-dose (7.6), indicating a dose-dependent reduction.
trap: Assuming that because significance was reported only for control versus high dose, only one dose lowered MDA, instead of reading the stepwise fall in means (12.5, 9.8, 7.6).

stem: Which follow-up experiment would give the strongest evidence that upregulation of endogenous superoxide dismutase (SOD) is required for the reduction in MDA produced by Antiox-7?

options.A: Randomize mice to Antiox-7 or placebo and measure MDA only.
options.B: Repeat the three-group design and measure SOD activity alongside MDA, without any other manipulation.
options.C: Give each mouse Antiox-7 and then placebo in sequence and measure MDA only.
options.D: Add a group given Antiox-7 plus an SOD inhibitor and compare its MDA with the Antiox-7-only group.

explanation: Correct: D. Blocking SOD while giving Antiox-7 tests necessity: if the MDA reduction disappears when SOD is inhibited, SOD is required. Why the others are wrong: A) Measuring MDA only cannot address any mechanism. B) Measuring SOD alongside MDA shows correlation, which does not show that SOD is required. C) A sequential design measuring MDA only has no mechanistic measurement and adds carryover problems.
trap: Choosing a correlational measurement when the question asks for evidence that a mechanism is required.

stem: Calculate the absolute difference in mean MDA between the control and high-dose groups.
explanation: Correct: C) 12.5 - 7.6 = 4.9 µmol/L. Why the others are wrong: A) 2.2 is low dose minus high dose (9.8 - 7.6). B) 2.7 is control minus low dose (12.5 - 9.8). D) 12.5 is the control mean alone, not a difference.
trap: Subtracting the wrong pair of groups, such as control minus low dose (2.7) or low dose minus high dose (2.2), instead of control minus high dose.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the data presented?

options.A: Mean MDA in the high-dose group was 4.9 µmol/L lower than in the control group.
options.B: Mean MDA fell at each step from control to low dose to high dose.
options.C: The SDs (0.9 to 1.2 µmol/L) were similar across the three groups.
options.D: Antiox-7 increased SOD enzyme activity in the treated mice.

explanation: Correct: D. Only plasma MDA was measured; SOD activity was not reported, so no effect on SOD can be concluded. Why the others are wrong: A) 12.5 - 7.6 = 4.9, so A is supported. B) 12.5, 9.8, 7.6 fall at each step, so B is supported. C) SDs of 1.2, 1.0 and 0.9 are similar, so C is supported.
trap: Assuming that a proposed mechanism was measured because the passage discusses oxidative stress.

stem: Plasma MDA was measured as an index of lipid peroxidation. What does the lower MDA in the Antiox-7 groups most directly indicate?

options.A: Less oxidative damage to membrane lipids
options.B: More oxidative damage to membrane lipids
options.C: Higher production of reactive oxygen species

explanation: Correct: A. MDA is a breakdown product of lipid peroxidation caused by reactive oxygen species, so lower MDA indicates less lipid oxidative damage. Why the others are wrong: B) Lower MDA means less, not more, peroxidation. C) More ROS would raise lipid peroxidation and MDA. D) Diet was not manipulated and MDA is not a measure of fat intake.
trap: Reading a lower marker value as a higher level of the process it measures.
